title: Stream abort confirmation, resume-jitter sampler, and idempotent tool-call tokens (OpenAI-bridge)
author: Aisha Patel
description: Motivation: We continue to see customer-visible flakiness around mid-stream client disconnects and tool/function-call replay behavior. Two recurring failure modes were: (1) clients issuing a cancel then reconnecting and triggering duplicate tool calls; (2) server hard-deadlines dropping in-flight streams without a clear client-visible confirmation, causing callers to retry blindly. This PR introduces a compact acknowledgment flow for client-initiated aborts, a resume-jitter sampler to reduce thundering reconnects, and an idempotency token propagation for function/tool calls. Goals: reduce duplicate tool executions, make abort semantics observable/explicit to clients, and smooth reconnect traffic so we avoid capacity spikes. Summary of changes: - wire a short-lived abort-ack token into the OpenAI-compat streaming handshake (client sends cancel -> server responds with abort_ack ID) - server emits an explicit "abort_confirmed" event down the stream before final closure, carrying an optional remediation attribute when a runtime snapshot was persisted - introduce a resume_jitter sampler at the client-proxy and edge layers (configurable base-window + randomized offset) to spread reconnects over a loose window - add an idempotency propagation header for tool/function calls (X-RW-Tool-Idempotency) that is validated by the tool-runner and used for safe dedup/replay - make server soft-deadline behavior negotiable: soft_deadline_ms may be advertised in the initial handshake; server will emit grace-warning events when approaching the soft deadline and perform a controlled checkpoint if configured - observability: new per-stream telemetry tags (abort_ack_id, resume_sampler_bucket, tool_idempotency_key) and an egress tracing span that correlates stream lifecycle events with tool runs - OpenAI-compat adapter mapping: map new abort_confirmed event to an extension field in JSON chunked responses so existing clients see a stable extinction marker Compatibility and safety notes: - Default behavior is opt-in: the abort-ack and idempotency headers are supported but not required. Existing clients should continue to operate unchanged. - Tool-runner dedup store is probabilistic (LRU TTL-backed) by default to stay bounded; customers can opt into a durable idempotency backend in Dedicated/Private. - Resume jitter defaults are conservative (50-500ms window) to avoid latency regressions on single-client reconnects Rollout plan: - Feature gate behind runtime flag + compatibility header. - Canary rollout in Hosted with 1% of streams for 48 hours, collecting duplication-rate and reconnect-splay histograms. - Gradually enable for Dedicated tenants after opt-in since it touches tool-runner behavior. Risks & mitigations: - Missing idempotency key could still produce duplicates; mitigated by instrumentation and clear client docs. - Poorly chosen jitter windows could increase tail latency; we provide telemetry and runtime knobs for tuning. The PR description below includes a short changelog, commits summary, files touched, reviewer conversation, CI summary and merge details.

review_comments: Diego Martinez: Can we make the abort_ack token size bounded and avoid allocating a new UUID per stream? Suggest we use a 128-bit truncated hash derived from stream id + epoch.
Aisha Patel: Good call — switched to 128-bit truncated HMAC(stream_id||server_epoch) in a1d9c7c and added unit tests. See commit a1d9c7c.
Lina Chen: We should be careful with the default dedup window in the dedup_cache; 5m might be too long for noisy workloads. Recommend 1m default with config knob.
Aisha Patel: lowered default to 1m and exposed RW_TOOL_DEDUP_TTL for Dedicated/Private customers.
Omar Singh: How do we surface abort_confirmed in the OpenAI adapter without breaking streaming parsers that expect only finish_reason? Consider extension field namespacing.
Aisha Patel: adapter now emits extension.redwood.abort_confirmed to avoid collisions; documented in docs/openai-compat/abort-and-resume.md
ci_checks: e2e: flaky (1 failed test) -> rerun -> pass
release_notes: Added abort-ack handshake, resume jitter sampling, and optional tool idempotency propagation. New OpenAI-compat extension: extension.redwood.abort_confirmed. Default behavior is opt-in behind feature flag.
